title: docs: a 30-second README demo GIF at the top of the README — the app runs, an agent creates a record over MCP, a read-only identity is refused — rendered by a committed script; plus the GitHub topics list for the maintainer to set
body:
立卡门类别 ③ — 维护者直派的任务 (maintainer-directed task).

## Maintainer ruling (verbatim, untranslated)

> 为什么别人星那么多，我们这么少

> 创建一个issue，派发处理 README 的 GIF 和 topics

Given in session https://claude.ai/code/session_011hRnra93sK5Q2gTYYTbdJR on 2026-10-08. The second line directs this card. The first is the question it answers: the PM's reading, which the maintainer accepted by directing the work, was that a visitor decides in thirty seconds on the README, that the README today opens on a static cover and a text walkthrough, and that the one thing that shows the four promises at once is a short recording of the loop the talk demonstrates: the app runs, an agent creates a record over MCP, the same call under a read-only identity is refused.

## Why

The README on main at 7b926f7600 opens on the slogan and the chip row, then a static cover image that links to the 90-second YouTube video, then the architecture diagram, then "Try it in five minutes" in prose. Nothing moves, and nothing shows an agent doing anything. A GitHub topic page sorted by stars lists 2,779 ontology repositories; the ones that gained thousands of stars in 2026 all open on something a visitor can watch. This card gives the README a thirty-second moving demo, generated by a committed script so it can be re-rendered when the Console changes, and records the topics the repository should carry so it is found under the words people search.

## Part A. The demo GIF (dev work, one draft PR)

A1. The recording, docs/screenshots/readme-demo.gif. An animated GIF, looping, 1200 px wide, 20 to 35 seconds, at most 3 MB (hard cap 4 MB; if the honest recording cannot fit, drop the frame rate or the duration, never the width below 1000 px, and report the final size). Three beats, each with a short on-frame caption in English:

1. The app runs. A typed object definition on screen for a moment (the example's own, a few fields, no scrolling), then the dev server starting and the Console's list view of that object in the browser.
2. An agent creates a record over MCP. A real MCP tools/call against the running app's /api/v1/mcp endpoint, shown as the request and the real response, then the Console refreshed with the new row visible (and the audit or created-by evidence if the Console shows one).
3. A read-only identity is refused. The same call under an identity whose permissions do not allow the create, the real refusal response, the Console unchanged.

Close on one frame: the slogan "The ontology is the software." and the four chips Executable · AI-writable · Agent-operable · You own it.

Honesty rules for the recording: every browser frame is a real screenshot of the real Console against a really running app; the agent beat is a real MCP call with the real response bytes; the terminal frames may be re-rendered from captured real output for legibility (typed effect, large monospace) but must not show output that did not occur; no fabricated chat transcript of any assistant, no invented records, no model identifiers anywhere in the frames or the caption. The caption calls the caller "an agent" or "any MCP client", which is what it is.

A2. The generator, docs/screenshots/render-readme-demo.mjs, in the style of docs/screenshots/render-hero-cover.mjs: header comment with usage and the refusals, resolves Playwright's chromium and sharp from the packages that already declare them (never runs playwright install; the browser binary is the preinstalled one under PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH), boots the chosen example app on an ephemeral state root, logs in with the seeded dev admin, mints the API keys it needs through the documented API, captures the frames, and assembles the GIF. Re-running it from a clean checkout must reproduce a GIF with the same beats (byte-identity is not required). Document the one-line command to re-render in the header and in the PR body.

A3. The README edit, README.md. The GIF becomes the first visual: directly under the chip row, centred, with a one-line caption under it naming the three beats. The YouTube line ("Watch: ObjectStack in 90 Seconds") stays as a text link under the caption. The static cover image is no longer embedded in the README; docs/screenshots/hero-cover-dark.png stays committed and untouched (it is the docs site's og:image). The architecture diagram and everything below it stay as they are. Alt text on the GIF describes the three beats for readers who do not see it.

## Part B. GitHub topics (maintainer action, outside git)

The fleet relay has no operation for repository topics (its operations are issue_create, issue_patch, labels_add, comment, comment_edit, pr_create, merge, transfer), and topics are repository settings, not files, so no PR can set them. The maintainer sets them on the repository page (About, the gear icon, Topics). Proposed list, lowercase, hyphenated, within GitHub's limit of twenty:

ontology · operational-ontology · executable-ontology · business-ontology · metadata-driven · ai-agents · agentic-ai · mcp · mcp-server · ai-native · enterprise-software · low-code · typescript · zod · palantir-alternative

palantir-alternative is optional: it is the topic the open-source Foundry look-alikes use and the one a search for alternatives lands on; drop it if the association is unwanted. While there, confirm the About description reads the descriptor sentence: One executable business ontology. AI writes it, the runtime runs it, agents operate it, you own it.

This part is not the dev's and does not block Part A. The card closes when the Part A PR lands; the landing comment repeats Part B for the maintainer.

## Guardrails for the author

- Surface: README.md (the top of the file only, nothing below the architecture diagram), docs/screenshots/readme-demo.gif (new, the one binary this card admits), docs/screenshots/render-readme-demo.mjs (new). No packages/** change: if the example app, the CLI or the MCP endpoint misbehaves in a way the recording needs fixed, stop, record the exact failure, and report it as a fork rather than patching around it. No apps/docs change, no content/** change, no CHANGELOG.md.
- Use what the repository already holds: the example apps under examples/ (app-crm, app-showcase, app-todo), objectstack dev with its seeded admin, the API-key path documented in content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx, Playwright from examples/app-showcase, sharp from the docs app. ffmpeg is present on this image at /usr/bin/ffmpeg; verify in your container before relying on it, and if it is absent say so in the report and use what is available. Adding a dependency to any package.json is a fork to report, not a decision to make.
- No model identifiers in the frames, the script, the README, the commits or the PR body.
- The README must keep passing its gates; derive the list with scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs from the real change set and run every one, including the published-links gate on the README.
- Changeset: nothing publishes; skip-changeset applies once packages/** is confirmed untouched.
- Serial constraint: PR #22224 (draft, another seat) edits the README's contributor-path section lower in the file. Branch from main; do not touch that section; if #22224 lands first, merge main into the branch before the final push and confirm the top of the README still reads as this card describes.

## Non-goals

- A Chinese README, a new 90-second video, or changes to the docs site. The GIF is for the README; whether the docs home also shows it is a later decision.
- A chat-transcript style demo of a named assistant. The agent beat is an MCP call, shown as such.
- The GitHub About description and topics are the maintainer's clicks (Part B), not a PR.

## Who acts

domain:devx lane, this seat, one os-dev dispatch at the default tier, one draft PR carrying the README edit, the script and the GIF. Base is origin/main at 7b926f7600. Precedent for a committed rendered asset with its generator: docs/screenshots/render-hero-cover.mjs and hero-cover-dark.png, landed by PR #21591.
